text:
priya: hitting a weird repro in the Go sampleapp — generator stream sometimes never returns when ctx is cancelled during an auth retry. can anyone sanity-check?

alex: hmm, is this the sample that uses the onboard example flow with refresh token middleware?

priya: yeah, the one in /examples/golang/generator-onboard. seq: request -> auth retry -> stream handshake -> ctx cancel. sometimes the recv goroutine keeps running.

mike: ugh goroutine leaks again. do you have a tiny repro snippet?

priya: trimmed down:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 1500*time.Millisecond)
defer cancel()
req := client.NewGenerateRequest(...)
stream, err := client.GenerateStream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { return err }
for {
  chunk, err := stream.Recv()
  if err != nil { break }
  // process
}
```
Cancel happens while auth middleware is retrying a 401 -> refresh flow. sometimes Recv() never returns.

sarah: does the auth retry block before creating the http request or after? if it spins in a goroutine without ctx it will leak.

priya: looks like our refresh function does internal sleeps/backoff that don't check ctx. hence the problem. but even if refresh checks ctx, the generator's read loop still hangs unless we close underlying transport.

alex: sounds like two issues: (1) auth retry/backoff should be cancelable, (2) generator stream should expose an explicit Close/Interrupt so callers can force-stop recv. Web SDK has abort controller parity; Go needs ergonomic pattern.

jen: agreed on parity. right now Go's generator API only takes ctx at call start but doesn't provide a mid-stream interrupt method. dev experience expects per-chunk context or an Abort() on the stream object.

mike: quick workaround: call stream.Close() from another goroutine on cancel. does our stream type implement Close()?

priya: not reliably. the userland wrapper has Close() but underlying http transport may still block. i tried closing the request body, but go http2 client blocks on active streams sometimes.

devops-bot: CI flaky test alert: example/generator-onboard now failing on linux-amd64 (timeout) — issue #2487 created.

alex: thanks for filing. proposal: make refreshToken(ctx) check ctx at every step, ensure backoffs use time.AfterContext (or select on ctx.Done), and add Stream.Interrupt() to signal underlying transport + cancel internal readers. that gives ergonomic parity with AbortController.

sarah: API sketch:
```go
type Stream interface {
  Recv() (*Chunk, error)
  Interrupt() error // forces underlying conn close and unblocks Recv
}
```
We should also document recommended pattern in onboarding: always pass ctx per-call and prefer Interrupt for mid-stream cancel.

jen: also call out common pitfall in sampleapp: "do not rely on defer cancel() inside long-running request handlers" — we should show a stop-wait pattern.

mike: can we add a tiny e2e test that simulates auth failure, slow refresh, cancel ctx and assert no leaked goroutines? that'll catch regressions.

priya: on it. i'll open a PR with: small API change + updated sample + e2e test + notes in devex onboarding doc. will link here.

alex: awesome. fyi keep changes minimal in public API — maybe add Interrupt as optional interface so existing users unaffected.

jen: ping me for docs review. i'll add a short snippet to onboarding and a badge showing "generator stream safe cancel" in the sample readme.

priya: filing the PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-inference/pull/4126 — includes test and sample tweak. thanks all :raised_hands:
